heading: Induction heads copy continuations by combining with earlier heads attending to previous tokens
definition: in small attention-only transformers, induction heads form by composing with an earlier previous-token head and implement [A][B] … [A] → [B].
summary: Several independent groups support this mechanism in small two-layer attention-only transformers, including evidence from blocking attention to the previous token during training. In language models, the order in which heads form is observed rather than experimentally tested, and path patching—intervening on specific connections between model components—shows that the simple circuit explains only part of induction behavior.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at toy scale for small two-layer attention-only models. R2 at <1B is supported narrowly by observational composition and formation-order evidence in a ~3.4M-parameter attention-only LM (arXiv:2402.02364#R1, arXiv:2402.02364#R5, arXiv:2402.02364#R7), without a causal formation test. ? at 1-10B: the previous R0 assignment relied on an out-of-scope Pythia model with MLPs (arXiv:2608.22007#A1-P28-5h). ? at 10-100B and >100B: neither has a key in counts: V1.studies_by_size. That key reports 'not stated' 43, '<1B' 6 and '1-10B' 1; these raw coverage counts do not establish corrected, architecture-specific replication levels.
suggested_status.reason: Independent attention-only evidence retains the basis for R2. In a two-layer bursty-Omniglot model, blocking Layer-1 previous-token attention during training prevents ICL (arXiv:2503.05631#r25). In a ~3.4M-parameter two-layer Pile-trained attention-only LM, weight-composition and head-score observations support the circuit and its developmental ordering; causal formation remains untested (arXiv:2402.02364#R1, arXiv:2402.02364#R5, arXiv:2402.02364#R7). Path patching qualifies the simple account: PTH-K explains 53.3% on the broader evaluation distribution (arXiv:2304.05969#R4); expanded All-Long paths leave approximately 24.1% unexplained on the induction subset, so this result is limits_scope rather than full recovery (arXiv:2304.05969#R14). GPT-2/Pythia MLP-model results provide neither support nor a scope limitation for literal V1: weight alignment measures potential wiring and head-output ablations measure copying effects without isolating the composition edge (arXiv:2608.22007#C1, arXiv:2608.22007#A1-G2-5). Raw counts: V1.verdicts.supports.studies 46, V1.verdicts.limits_scope.studies 18, V1.verdicts.challenges.studies 0; V1.tested_with_controls 35; V1.tested_with_code 24; V1.tested_by_review_class.reviewed 15. These are supplied pre-correction counts, not corrected totals.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would causal composition tests across other natural-text attention-only seeds, depths and widths reproduce the mechanism and the need for additional paths? A controlled failure in the specified architecture would support reconsidering C. Size-specific causal tests in attention-only models would clarify the scale ratings. Resolve author overlap before treating all linked studies as independent (counts: V1.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original 2).

original_result.setup: The original study tracked induction-head scores, in-context learning (learning from the current context), and training loss in ordinary one-layer models.
original_result.result: Induction heads never formed, in-context learning never substantially developed, and the loss bump was absent. Models with more than one layer showed the reported transition.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Two-layer transformers learned previous-token and induction heads on tasks using randomly chosen cue (trigger) tokens.
On examples testing induction, previous-token composition and other circuit paths explained most loss changes.
Previous-token attention and attention retrieving labels emerged together with classification using examples in the context.
GPT-2 Small used previous-token features to drive induction copying.
Head ablations identified repeated-pattern copying in a two-layer attention-only transformer.
Attention to parent (conditioning) tokens, then matching, estimated token transitions through induction.
RegBench transformers composed earlier previous-token heads with a later context-matching head.
In GELU-2L (two layers), induction features tracked copying the continuations of earlier matching sequences.
During language-model training, induction heads learned to build keys using outputs from earlier previous-token heads.
One-layer induction required exponentially greater resources than cited two-layer constructions.
Two-layer Llama-style transformers learned synthetic induction perfectly while one-layer models struggled.
Relative positional encoding preserved previous-token associations and accurate repeated-pattern completion.
Markov-trained transformers learned previous-token attention, then attention to tokens following matches.
On Omniglot (handwritten characters), a two-layer transformer's previous-token heads supplied information for induction matching.
A small attention-only transformer implemented induction through a composed two-step circuit.
NanoGPT copy and search heads retrieved the expected tokens during deductive reasoning.
Embeddings built to carry previous-token information enabled single-layer induction copying.
Markov-trained attention-only transformers learned the previous-token component of an induction circuit.
Previous-token heads formed before attention extended to longer histories in trigram learning.
Models generalizing beyond training examples on Markov-chain tasks showed induction-like attention patterns.
A circuit described by three parameters could retrieve previous items in attention-only transformers.
Previous-token and induction heads emerged during in-context transitive inference.
Early learning from context on Omniglot (handwritten characters) required previous-token attention and two layers.
During associative recall, attention that copies and attention that selects emerged in successive layers.
Two-layer Markov models learned to aggregate preceding-token information, then perform matching resembling induction.
A simplified transformer converged to heads copying conditioning (parent) tokens, followed by matching token histories.
Attention maps showed items paired with labels, followed by attention that matched and copied labels.
Omniglot (handwritten-character) GPT-2 models learned previous-token attention, then attention retrieving the correct label.
Previous-token heads preceded induction in two-layer synthetic-language models.
Strong multimodal learning from examples in context required both previous-token heads and induction heads.
Random input-output mapping tasks produced strong previous-token and induction heads under varied training constraints.
GMC-trained Llama 3 and GPT-2 learned successive previous-token and induction attention.
On Markov tasks, heads copying tokens from fixed earlier offsets fed a later matching head.
Previous-token heads causally contributed to induction in small masked diffusion models.
Pythia ablations identified previous-token and induction heads as necessary just after ignition.
Cellular-automaton transformers moved information between spatial positions, then matched against earlier examples.
Ablating an attention-only head sharply reduced code-like induction accuracy.
A two-layer attention-only model boosted the probability of repeated-pattern continuations for nearly every token.
An attention-only docstring circuit used induction attention with a substantial causal effect.
GELU-2L (two layers) had induction features that depended on both previous-token heads and induction heads.
Previous-token heads developed before later-layer prefix matching in attention-only language models.
Induction formed only when heads could read earlier head outputs.
Previous-token, matching, and readout parameters preserved nearly all bigram in-context performance.
Full-attention transformers showed previous-token sensitivity, with information transfer developing before matching.
Refined induction circuits retained previous-token head outputs feeding keys and recovered most performance.
GPT-2 Small induction heads had strong connections from previous-token heads and contributed substantially to copying.
Training with fixed cue (trigger) tokens restricted induction to triggers encountered during training.
The minimal circuit with two heads explained little behavior across the model's full data distribution.
Linking previous-token heads in sequence enabled matching prefixes consisting of two tokens.
A two-layer Llama-style transformer with hidden representations of size 8 learned induction poorly.
Absolute positional encoding weakened previous-token attention and induction at later positions.
Induction on Omniglot (handwritten characters) also needed value contributions from heads lacking previous-token attention.
Transitive inference also needed a head that routed information but had weak induction strength.
A construction for higher-order induction used nonlinearities to rebuild representations for matching.
The proof of training convergence assumed position information initially biased toward conditioning (parent) tokens.
GPT-2 image-label retrieval weakened later in training alongside declining in-context learning.
Alternative positional encodings preserved induction peaks while yielding more diffuse attention patterns.
At finite scale, induction attention blended partial context matches into smoothed n-gram predictions.
Masked diffusion induction also needed heads attending to next tokens and outputs feeding attention queries.
Simple previous-token composition recovered little performance until additional pathways were included.
Induction copying varied across tokens and raised probabilities for tokens with similar output (unembedding) vectors.
The docstring head performed induction only for selected destination tokens.
Naive previous-token composition recovered only partial performance and required additional attention pathways.
Copying persisted after previous-token head ablation and relied on broader machinery in larger models.

untested.what: A quantitative causal test of previous-token-head → induction-head K-composition in more than one natural-text-trained attention-only model, or across seeds or sizes of such models. The causal tests in the pack each use a single 2-layer OpenWebText model, possibly the same one in all three. attn-only-4l has only a qualitative identification of previous-token head 0.2.
untested.basis: Untested and problems lines: lw:j6s9H9SHrEhEfuJnq ('any model other than this single 2-layer attention-only model'); arXiv:2304.05969 ('Only one 2-layer attention-only shortformer model'); lw:JvZhhzycHu2Yd57RN ('No check across several small models'); lw:u6KXXmKFbXfWzoAXn (no quantitative composition test); arXiv:2402.02364 problems (one run). counts: V1.studies_by_size 'not stated': 43.

untested.what: A causal test that induction heads form through composition during natural-text training of attention-only models, for example blocking previous-token attention during LM training. This has been done only on synthetic data (arXiv:2503.05631#r25). Formation evidence on the Pile is observational.
untested.basis: arXiv:2402.02364 verdict reason ('No causal ablation was run'); lw:Zza9MNA7YtHkzAtit untested line ('no ablation'); arXiv:2410.02984 untested line (causal composition not tested). counts: V1.main_rows_by_operation.training is 10 rows.

untested.what: Attention-only models deeper than 4 layers, or swept in width or size. The attention-only subjects in the pack have 2, 3 or 4 layers. The deeper or width-swept models (8-layer, up to 32-layer, hidden-size sweeps) all have MLPs.
untested.basis: Pack subjects: arXiv:2607.15893 (L2, L3), lw:nuJFTS5iiJKT5G5yh and lw:u6KXXmKFbXfWzoAXn (attn-only-4l); arXiv:2602.07562#R6 (depth up to 32, with FFN), arXiv:2411.19574#R7 (width, with MLPs). counts do not break out attention-only models.

untested.what: Direct causal isolation of previous-token-head → induction-head composition above 2.8B parameters, or in chat/instruct or fine-tuned models. These are extensions beyond V1's stated small attention-only setting. Larger-model weight mapping and subspace interventions do not establish this direct causal composition test.
untested.basis: counts: V1.studies_by_size has '<1B': 6 and '1-10B': 1 and no '10-100B' or '>100B' key; V1.studies_by_stage has only 'other' 39, 'not stated' 10 and 'base' 2. These metadata do not distinguish attention-only models or direct composition interventions. arXiv:2608.22007#A1-P28-5h reports five-head ablation destroying 41.3% of copying gain in Pythia-2.8B, an MLP model outside V1. The checks.json correction for V1.untested[3] states that community/head-set ablations stop at 2.8B, while Pythia-6.9B has weight mapping and two-dimensional subspace deletion; direct previous-token-to-induction causal composition above 2.8B is not demonstrated.

untested.what: An extension of arXiv:2409.10559's staged-gradient-flow formation guarantee beyond Assumption 3.3's parent-biased RPE initialization. The theorem concerns a stylized two-attention-layer transformer with an FFN on Markov data; it does not demonstrate formation failure without that initialization (arXiv:2409.10559#r1). The cited n=2 experiment measures first-layer copier formation, leaving complete previous-token-head → matcher composition undetermined by that measurement (arXiv:2409.10559#r3).
untested.basis: V1.against[8] and checks.json for arXiv:2409.10559: label l1 distinguishes an assumption limiting the guarantee from demonstrated failure; the r3 correction identifies an FFN, n=2, and a copier-only measurement. The l0 correction separates the theoretical n=1 specialization from the n=2 simulations and states that no joint-training n=1 result is reported. counts: V1.main_rows_by_operation.training does not distinguish initialization assumptions, FFN inclusion, or component measurements from complete-circuit tests.

wording_issues.phrase: composing with an earlier previous-token head
wording_issues.issue: The phrase leaves additional query/value paths unspecified. In a two-layer attention-only OpenWebText model, the naive combined Q/K/V account recovers 35% of loss, and the embeddings-to-query hypothesis recovers 51% (lw:j6s9H9SHrEhEfuJnq#r8, #r6). In the two-layer attention-only Omniglot model, copying uses V-composition from non-previous-token Layer-1 heads; ablating those heads with Layer-2 attention patterns preserved leaves 34.27% accuracy, and previous-token-to-induction wiring is many-to-many (arXiv:2404.07129#r7, #r9). In small attention-only absorbing-mask diffusion LMs evaluated on repeated random tokens, next-token pathways also contribute, and composition enters both queries and keys at masked query positions (arXiv:2607.15893#r04, #r28). These results qualify the bare circuit account without showing that previous-token composition is absent.

The evidence distinguishes observed formation order from causal formation tests. In the Pile-trained two-layer attention-only language model, previous-token scores rise before prefix-matching scores, but no causal intervention on induction-circuit formation is reported (arXiv:2402.02364#R5, #R7). In the synthetic bursty-Omniglot two-layer attention-only model, blocking Layer-1 previous-token attention during training prevents ICL from emerging (arXiv:2503.05631#r25). The latter supplies causal formation evidence in its synthetic setting; the natural-text observations alone do not establish that composition causes formation.

The shorthand omits longer-context and soft matching. In the two-layer attention-only OpenWebText model, path patching uses a K = 3 query/key context window (arXiv:2304.05969#R11). Expanded All-Long paths still leave approximately 24.1% unexplained on the induction subset, a partial explanation (arXiv:2304.05969#R14). In two-layer disentangled attention-only order-2 Markov models, finite attention scale produces substantial attention to partial context matches under the no-BOS independent prior and the hierarchical prior even with BOS; these results qualify strict copying (arXiv:2607.02800#R2, #R4). In the canonical two-layer attention-only model, copying also boosts tokens near B in unembedding space (lw:DgMH6kcsqypycF5mT#r4). In synthetic triggered-bigram models trained with fixed triggers, the second-layer head is trigger-specific (arXiv:2306.00802#R4).

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation token subset (induction-selected vs all tokens)
method_sensitivity.what: In arXiv:2304.05969's two-layer attention-only model, All-Long explains approximately 75.9% on the induction subset: AUE 0.219 against ATE 0.907, leaving 24.1% unexplained (R14). This is partial recovery and a scope limitation. All-Long explains 55.2% on the first 300 tokens of held-out OpenWebText (R12); the separately reported full-set AUE is 0.244 against ATE 0.432 (R13). The repeats subset has AUE 0.777 against ATE 1.444 (R15), but selects previously occurring uncommon tokens without isolating prefix matching, so this row alone cannot determine V1. lw:j6s9H9SHrEhEfuJnq reports lower recovery when evaluated on all tokens (r29).

method_sensitivity.factor: Hypothesis specificity (which paths are kept in causal scrubbing or path patching)
method_sensitivity.what: lw:j6s9H9SHrEhEfuJnq reports recovery of 35% (naive, r8), 62% (r12), 76% (r16), 86% (r24) and 89% (r28); lw:JvZhhzycHu2Yd57RN reports 35% to 86% (r1, r2). In arXiv:2304.05969's two-layer attention-only model, comparable component refinements are Direct-V 64.1% to Positional-V 86.2% (R2, R6); Direct-Q 48.7% to Positional-Q 72.6% (R3, R7); and Positional-K, combining positional query and key paths, 52.5% to Long-QK 59.5% with window K = 3 (R8, R11). Combined hypotheses explain 28.2% for All-Initial, 48.6% for All-Positional, 55.2% for All-Long and 73.5% for All-Final (R5, R9, R12, R16). Different components are separate comparisons; the expanded account remains incomplete.

In arXiv:2412.11459's two-layer transformers, APE versus RPE changes previous-token attention at evaluation positions t<256: 0.1979 versus 0.9337 (R6, R10). RPE uses fixed random relative key vectors. In arXiv:2511.08854's two-layer, one-head-per-layer attention-only transformer (d_model 16), omitting positional encoding before Q0 drops m→s1 attention from 1.0 to 0.0941 on the synthetic s-m-…-s induction task (r4).

method_sensitivity.factor: Architecture: depth and how previous-token information reaches the induction head
method_sensitivity.what: One versus two layers changes whether induction forms in arXiv:2306.00802's synthetic transformers (R1, R3). Parallel versus sequential one-layer attention changes whether induction forms on lw:tiEgivi7crHSnSrH5's synthetic repeated-block task (r2, r3); the sequential result remains observed for V1. A hard-wired previous-token embedding lets arXiv:2512.18634's single-layer model implement matching and copying (r2), without testing formation through composition with a learned earlier previous-token head.

arXiv:2404.07129: previous-token-head ablation leaves accuracy of 99.85% with Layer-2 patterns preserved and 69.87% with values preserved (r5, r6); ablating other heads leaves 34.27% versus 99.32%, respectively (r7, r8). Single Layer-2 head ablations cause virtually no decrease, while keeping one head gives 98% (r3, r4). In arXiv:2506.04289's two-layer attention-only transitive-inference model, removing low-induction-strength Layer-2 head 4 significantly degrades performance; other individual Layer-2 ablations have minimal impact (R3, R4). This does not determine whether V1 composition is incomplete. In lw:nuJFTS5iiJKT5G5yh's attn-only-4l, head 1.4, 120 constructed code-like prompts have clean reference probability 0.28. Ablation at the induction position lowers probability by approximately 20 percentage points, versus below 5 percentage points at other positions (r3, r4).

With fixed triggers, the second-layer head is trigger-specific; with random triggers it is generic in arXiv:2306.00802's synthetic transformers (R4, R5). In arXiv:2607.02800's two-layer disentangled attention-only transformers on order-2 Markov tasks, BOS presence and the task prior change whether matching is exact or smoothed (R2, R3, R4). At finite attention scale, the no-BOS independent-prior condition and the hierarchical-prior condition even with BOS attend to partial as well as full context matches, giving partial realization of strict copying. The no-BOS copy heads were initialized rather than shown to emerge from scratch. Induction strength varies with token identity in lw:DgMH6kcsqypycF5mT (r1).

In arXiv:2503.05631's two-layer attention-only transformer trained on bursty Omniglot, Layer 1 switches away from previous-token attention later in training as in-context learning gives way to context-dependent in-weights learning (r2). Layer-2 induction heads remain largely unchanged; the strategy switch occurs in Layer 1.

method_sensitivity.factor: Ablation target and model/checkpoint context in architectural extensions
method_sensitivity.what: In arXiv:2608.22007's GPT-2 small, mean-ablating L4H11 destroys 1.9% of clean induction gain; ablating community heads excluding induction heads destroys 77.3%. Pythia-160M five-head ablation destroys 60.0%. In arXiv:2607.27281's just-post-ignition Pythia-70M, previous-token and induction heads are individually necessary; Pythia-160M reports necessary-set size 2 without independently identifying members. Composition is not isolated. GPT-2/Pythia have MLPs, outside V1. In arXiv:2601.20796's multimodal two-layer decoder with MLPs, previous-token knockout changes ICL accuracy from 0.970 to 0.199, also outside V1. In arXiv:2607.15893's folded no-LayerNorm attention-only diffusion model (L2 run A), trained on FineWeb-Edu and evaluated on synthetic repeated random tokens, previous-token ablation drops induction score by 2.10 nats (r03). These unmatched interventions, checkpoints and measures do not establish a V1 conflict; V1 does not require individual-head necessity.
